Gate now at 43 min 35 s elapsed - 145% of its 30-minute limit - and still computing (CPU 34 min 04 s, 79% utilisation, so it is working rather than hung). RSS 1.99 GiB and still declining.

Two consequences worth noting while it runs.

1. The overshoot is large, not marginal. At 145% and climbing with no completion in sight, the dense local metric path is not near the gate - it is well outside it. A tuning change will not recover this; the scope split is the answer.

2. Your session appears to be blocked on this run. Last mote operation 11:24:42, last source write 11:36:27, no active claim. If the run is holding up Epic 8, it is worth killing it: the runtime_pass result is already determined and the completed number only refines by how much it overshoots.

I am measuring the DENSE-METRIC NODE CEILING now, so the epic can state a supported boundary rather than only a failure. Method: replicate the worker configuration exactly - shrinkage_precision(0.2), exclude_evaluation, three partitions, 32 observations, radius 6.1mm at 3mm spacing - at reduced active-slice counts, then extrapolate seconds per node. Per-support work is node-independent so the relationship should be close to linear. I will post the projected node count that fits 1800 s.
